```toml
# LAN devices channel for television (tv)
# Fuzzy-search local network devices with open ports, MAC/vendor,
# hostname, latency, and last-seen timestamp.
#
# Usage:
#   tv lan-devices
#   lanscan                 # shell alias, runs a full scan up front
#
# The channel reads ~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv, which is populated by
# ~/.config/television/lan-scan.sh. `watch = 2.0` makes rows appear as
# the background scan progresses (state column: discovered / scanning /
# scanned / stale).
#
# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
#   1. All discovered devices (sorted by IP)
#   2. Only devices with open ports
#   3. Fresh only (last-seen within 5 min)
#
# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
#   1. Cached nmap service detail (fast)
#   2. Live `nmap -sV -Pn` rescan (blocking)
#   3. ARP + rDNS + mDNS metadata
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid tmux/TV conflicts):
#   Enter      Full `nmap -sV -A` in execute mode
#   Alt+R      Rescan ports on selected host + reload
#   Alt+F      Rescan full subnet (discover + ports) + reload
#   Alt+D      Re-discover only (no port scan) + reload
#   Alt+S      Open ssh to host
#   Alt+H      Open http://host in browser
#   Alt+C      Clear cache + reload
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)

[metadata]
name = "lan-devices"
description = "LAN devices: IP, MAC, vendor, hostname, open ports, latency"
requirements = ["nmap"]

[source]
# Columns (tab-separated, matches lan-scan.sh TSV_HEADER):
# 0:ip  1:mac  2:vendor  3:hostname  4:ports  5:top  6:rtt  7:seen  8:state
command = [
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  if [ ! -s "$tsv" ]; then
    "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh" all >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    printf '...\\t-\\t(scanning — results will stream in)\\t-\\t-\\t-\\t-\\t-\\tscanning\\n'
    exit 0
  fi
  awk -F'\\t' 'NR>1' "$tsv"
  """,
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  awk -F'\\t' 'NR>1 && $5 ~ /^[1-9]/' "$tsv"
  """,
  """
  tsv="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv"
  now=$(date +%s)
  awk -F'\\t' -v now="$now" 'NR>1 {
    "date -j -f %H:%M:%S \"" $8 "\" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -d \"" $8 "\" +%s 2>/dev/null" | getline ts
    if (now - ts < 300) print
  }' "$tsv"
  """,
]
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  [{split:\\t:4}p] {split:\\t:5}  {split:\\t:6}ms  {split:\\t:7}  {split:\\t:8}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
watch = 2.0
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  f="$HOME/.cache/tv/lan-ports/$ip.txt"
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then
    cat "$f"
  else
    echo "No cached port scan for $ip."
    echo "Press Alt+R to scan this host, or Ctrl+F to cycle preview."
  fi
  """,
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  echo "# Live nmap -sV -Pn -F $ip (blocking, ~10-30s)"
  echo
  nmap -sV -Pn -F "$ip" 2>/dev/null
  """,
  """
  ip='{split:\\t:0}'
  echo "# ARP"
  if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then arp -an | grep -F "($ip)" || echo "no ARP entry"; \
  else ip neigh show "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "no ARP entry"; fi
  echo
  echo "# Reverse DNS"
  getent hosts "$ip" 2>/dev/null || dig +short +time=1 +tries=1 -x "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"
  echo
  echo "# mDNS"
  if command -v avahi-resolve >/dev/null 2>&1; then avahi-resolve -a "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"; \
  elif [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then dscacheutil -q host -a ip_address "$ip" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"; \
  else echo "(no mDNS tool)"; fi
  echo
  echo "# Ping"
  ping -c 2 "$ip" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 5
  """,
]
header = "Device {split:\\t:0} ({split:\\t:2} / {split:\\t:3})"

[ui]
input_header = "LAN Devices"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 55

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:details"
alt-r = ["actions:rescan_host", "reload_source"]
alt-f = ["actions:rescan_all", "reload_source"]
alt-d = ["actions:rediscover", "reload_source"]
alt-s = "actions:ssh"
alt-h = "actions:http"
alt-c = ["actions:clean", "reload_source"]
ctrl-y = ["actions:copy_ip", "reload_source"]

[actions.details]
description = "Full nmap -sV -A scan"
command = "ip='{split:\\t:0}'; echo \"# nmap -sV -A $ip\"; nmap -sV -A -Pn \"$ip\" 2>/dev/null; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.rescan_host]
description = "Rescan selected host's open ports"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh ports --host '{split:\\t:0}' >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.rescan_all]
description = "Rescan full subnet (discover + ports)"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh all >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.rediscover]
description = "Re-discover hosts (no port scan)"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh discover >/dev/null 2>&1 &"
mode = "fork"

[actions.ssh]
description = "SSH to selected host"
command = "ssh '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.http]
description = "Open http://host in browser"
command = """
ip='{split:\\t:0}'
url="http://$ip"
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then open "$url"
elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null 2>&1; then xdg-open "$url"
else echo "No browser opener; URL: $url"; read -r _
fi
"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clean]
description = "Clear LAN scan cache"
command = "$HOME/.config/television/lan-scan.sh clean >/dev/null 2>&1"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_ip]
description = "Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)"
command = """
d='{split:\\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\\033]52;c;%s\\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
"""
mode = "fork"

```

Done. Summary of what's in place:

**Files created/modified**
- `dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh` — discovery + enrichment + port-scan orchestrator with a mkdir-based lock, sudo-gated fallback (`arp-scan` → `nmap -sn` + ARP cache), OUI vendor lookup, serial enrichment (rDNS/mDNS/RTT), incremental TSV writes.
- `dot_config/television/cable/lan-devices.toml` — TV channel with `watch = 2.0` cache-tail source, 3 source variants (all / with-ports / fresh), 3 preview variants (cached nmap / live rescan / ARP+DNS+ping), and `Alt+R/F/D/S/H/C` + `Ctrl+Y` keybindings.
- `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` — adds `lanscan` and `tv-lan` aliases.
- Docs: `docs/tools/tv.md` (new `lan-devices` section), `docs/tools/networking.md`, `docs/zsh/aliases.md`, `README.md`.

**Verified on your Mac**
- Subnet auto-detected as `192.168.168.0/24`.
- Discovered 6 hosts with vendor (Huawei / Raspberry Pi), hostnames (homerouter.cpe, raspberrypi, macbookpro, ipad, iphone), RTT.
- Port scan on `192.168.168.1` found `53/tcpwrapped, 80/http, 443/tcpwrapped`; cached detail written to `~/.cache/tv/lan-ports/192.168.168.1.txt`.
- `tv list-channels | grep lan-devices` shows the channel registered.

**UX for "scan takes time"**
- First open with empty cache: channel kicks off `lan-scan.sh all` in the background and shows a `scanning — results will stream in` placeholder; `watch = 2.0` pulls new rows in every 2s.
- `state` column transitions `discovered` → `scanning` → `scanned` so you can see progress per row.
- `Alt+R` rescans just the selected host; `Alt+F` triggers a full rescan; both reload the source immediately.

Try it: `tv lan-devices` (or `tv-lan`). First run will take ~30–60s on no-sudo; if you `sudo -v` first the `arp-scan` path kicks in and discovery drops to a couple of seconds.
